feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 2 (60 mm span, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.05) restored oval progress to 0.405 and s-bend to 0.423, while line losses held at 1.0 to 1.2. Iteration 0 (40 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y = 0.05) reached oval progress 0.664. That gap is the question this iteration tests: the wider span, the 16 mm footprint, or both. Iteration 1 showed that shortening the lead to y = 0.03 collapses progress, so the lead should stay at 0.05. I kept the controller gains at the iteration 2 values (kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45), which I scaled up when the span widened from 40 to 60 mm, so the footprint change is the only variable. max_error has sat at 0.0615 to 0.065 m across iterations 0, 1 and 2, so it does not respond to span, footprint or lead alone. Decide from the next race as follows. If oval progress rises above about 0.45 with line losses near 1, the footprint was blurring the signal: keep sensor_size 0.012 and try the wheel_track change to address max_error. If progress stays at or below about 0.4, the footprint is not the limit and the span is the likely cause, so try the narrower span below.
requested_changes: If oval progress rises above about 0.45 with line losses near 1, keep sensor_size 0.012 and set wheel_track to 0.10. max_error has stayed at 0.0615 to 0.065 m across iterations 0 to 2, so turn rate is the untested lever for it.

If progress stays at or below about 0.4 on the oval, keep sensor_size 0.012 and y 0.05 but narrow the span to x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025 (50 mm span). Iteration 0 used a 40 mm span at y 0.05 and reached oval progress 0.664, while iteration 2 used 60 mm and reached 0.405. The 50 mm span tests whether the wider array is what cost progress, and it should still cover the tape edge at 12 mm footprints.
Do not change the lead from y = 0.05. Iteration 1 showed that y = 0.03 cuts progress sharply (oval 0.273), and iteration 2 showed that restoring y = 0.05 recovers it (oval 0.405).
